title: The Question I Ask Every New Client
excerpt: It's not "what do you want" — it's a harder one, and it usually gets a more honest answer.
content:
Almost everyone can answer "what do you want" with something socially acceptable — more money, more balance, a promotion. The question that actually gets somewhere is "what are you willing to give up for it?"

That's usually where the real conversation starts.

title: Burnout Isn't a Time-Management Problem
excerpt: Most of my burned-out clients don't need a better calendar. They need a different job, or a different boundary.
content: I used to give burned-out clients productivity systems. It rarely worked, because the problem usually wasn't their calendar — it was a role, a boss, or a boundary that needed to change, not a better to-do list.
